s1.syndrome_frame: febrile illness with skin lesions in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: tender annular erythematous plaques on the neck and trunk
abnormal laboratory findings including leukopenia, anemia, and thrombocytopenia
key_facts: 10-day history of fever
tender lesions on the neck and trunk
past medical history of IgG-κ multiple myeloma
recent chemotherapy with ixazomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone
annular erythematous plaques with violaceous and crusted centers
white blood cell count: 2.3 × 10^3/μL
hemoglobin: 12.1 g/dL
platelet count: 29 × 10^3/μL
C-reactive protein: 3.31 mg/dL
blood culture: negative
skin biopsy showed inflammatory infiltrate of predominantly mononuclear cells
immunohistochemistry positive for CD68 and myeloperoxidase, negative for CD138

shortlist.label: Sweet syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: fever, tender skin lesions, and recent chemotherapy

shortlist.label: Neutrophilic eccrine hidradenitis
shortlist.why_kept: febrile illness, skin lesions, and recent chemotherapy

shortlist.label: Erythema multiforme
shortlist.why_kept: annular erythematous plaques with violaceous and crusted centers

shortlist.label: Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: immunocompromised patient with skin lesions and recent chemotherapy

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of fever, tender lesions on the neck and trunk, and laboratory findings of a low white blood cell count, elevated C-reactive protein, and negative blood culture, along with skin biopsy showing an inflammatory infiltrate of predominantly mononuclear cells and immunohistochemistry positive for CD68 and myeloperoxidase, are consistent with Sweet syndrome, particularly in the context of recent chemotherapy for multiple myeloma.

rejected.label: Neutrophilic eccrine hidradenitis
rejected.why: While it can occur in the setting of chemotherapy, the clinical presentation and biopsy findings do not specifically support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Erythema multiforme
rejected.why: The lesions described do not have the characteristic targetoid appearance of erythema multiforme, and the biopsy findings do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
rejected.why: The biopsy findings mention nuclear dust without obvious leukocytoclastic vasculitis, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and biopsy findings, including the lack of CD138 positivity, do not support this diagnosis.
